sections.h2: Why Galloway's size matters to a seller
sections.html:
Galloway Township is the largest municipality in New Jersey by area, so two houses with a Galloway address can sit miles apart and draw very different buyers. Total area is 114.49 square miles, of which 88.67 are land and 25.82 are water.

The township has an estimated 38,380 residents in 2025, up from 37,813 at the 2020 census. That is only 426.5 people per square mile. Galloway works as a growing edge city next to Atlantic City.

For 2020 to 2024, 79.8% of housing is owner-occupied, the median home value is $298,900 and median gross rent is $1,619. The township has no single downtown. Buyers search by community: Absecon Highlands, Cologne, Germania, Leeds Point, Oceanville, Pomona, Smithville and the Stockton University campus area. Older deeds may also use names such as Higbeetown, Pinehurst and Somersville.

sections.h2: What inspection does Galloway require on a resale?
sections.html:
Every residential resale needs a fire certificate covering smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers only. Township code Chapter 153 requires the inspection before the new owners occupy the dwelling.

The application, inspection and certificate go through the Fire Department at 300 E. Jimmie Leeds Road. The fee depends on how much notice you give, so ask for the inspection as soon as you have a closing date.

Fire certificate fees by notice before the change of ownership
When the request is receivedFee
More than 10 business days before the change of ownership$45
Four to 10 business days before$90
Fewer than four business days before$161

Violating the ordinance can bring a fine of up to $2,000, up to 90 days in jail or community service, and each day counts as a separate offense. The resale inspection stays limited to the three fire safety items and does not cover the rest of the house.

Rentals follow a separate and fuller inspection than resales. Under the rental ordinance, a certificate of occupancy is required on any rental, renewed every year or at each new occupant, whichever comes first, at $50 per inspection.

  • The lease must accompany the application and list every occupant's name and age.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are required in every rental unit.
  • A detached one- or two-family rental needs a fire extinguisher of at least 2A:10B:C and at most 10 pounds, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen with its top no higher than five feet from the floor.
  • A rental with a fireplace needs a chimney certification and proof that the dryer vent has been cleaned, or a notarized letter from the owner.
  • More than two follow-up inspections trigger another $50 fee.

The Housing Department handles applications at (609) 652-3700, extensions 241 or 249. Inspection requests must be emailed to the Construction office at inspect@gtnj.org with the permit number, address, type of inspection and your phone number.

Much of Galloway lies inside protected land, and some parcels carry extra rules. The township is one of 56 South Jersey municipalities in the Pinelands National Reserve, a 1.1 million acre area Congress established in 1978, and parts of Galloway also fall in the state-designated Pinelands Area. Ask the Community Development office whether your parcel is in that area before you promise a buyer an addition or a new outbuilding.

The homeowner, not the contractor, is responsible for obtaining a permit. Residential contractors need a state Consumer Affairs 13VH number, so keep contractor names and permit numbers for any work you had done before selling.

sections.h2: What nonresident owners owe on a sale
sections.html:
A nonresident seller prepays estimated gross income tax at the closing table. The formula multiplies the gain by 10.75%, but the payment can never be below 2% of the consideration written in the deed, even if there is no gain.

The payment goes with the deed and the GIT/REP-1 form to the Atlantic County Clerk, who forwards it to the state. A seller who wants to avoid delays can prepay at a Division of Taxation regional office and receive a stamped GIT/REP-2 before closing.

  • A New Jersey resident signs the GIT/REP-3 instead and pays nothing up front.
  • A nonresident can still use the GIT/REP-3 if one of its listed assurances fits, such as a deed for $1,000 or less or a settlement with no net proceeds to the seller.
  • Selling a principal residence that qualifies under Internal Revenue Code section 121 is another listed assurance, when the entire gain can be excluded.

The GIT/REP Unit answers questions at 609-322-9275. Call at least two weeks before a complicated closing.

Buyers care about the Garden State Parkway. It runs 5.7 miles through the township, with Interchange 40 for U.S. Route 30, Interchange 41 for Jimmie Leeds Road and Interchange 44 for Pomona. Route 50 and County Routes 561, 563 and 575 also cross the township, and NJ Transit buses 508, 554 and 559 reach Atlantic City. The mean commute is 23.6 minutes.

Stockton University sits in the Pomona section, which keeps a steady pool of renters nearby. A house bought as a rental brings the inspection rules above into play.

sections.h2: A sensible order for a quick sale
sections.html:
Book the fire inspection the moment you have a closing date, because the fee rises as the date gets closer. Test your smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and check the extinguisher yourself. If the house is a rental, gather the lease and the latest certificate of occupancy for the buyer. Then have your closing attorney prepare the deed and the GIT/REP form that fits you, resident or nonresident, and file both with the Atlantic County Clerk.

Because Galloway is so spread out, tell a buyer exactly which part of the township the house is in. A buyer comparing a Pomona address with one in Leeds Point is looking at very different surroundings, and the fire certificate, permit history and any Pinelands limits follow the parcel, not the town name. A cash buyer will usually ask for the same documents a financed buyer does: the deed, permit records, any rental certificate and proof that the fire inspection passed.

If anything fails the fire inspection, the usual fixes are inexpensive, such as a new detector battery or a replacement extinguisher. Fix the item and ask for a re-check rather than waiting for the buyer to raise it.

faqs.q: Does Galloway Township require an inspection to sell a house?
faqs.a: Yes, a fire certificate. Galloway inspects smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and fire extinguishers on every residential resale, and it must be done before the new owners occupy the home.

faqs.q: What does the Galloway Township resale fire certificate cost?
faqs.a: It costs $45 when the request arrives more than 10 business days before the change of ownership, $90 for four to 10 business days, and $161 for fewer than four business days.

faqs.q: Where do I apply for the Galloway Township fire certificate?
faqs.a: The Fire Department at 300 E. Jimmie Leeds Road handles the application, inspection and certificate. The Housing Department can be reached at (609) 652-3700, extensions 241 or 249.

faqs.q: How much tax does a nonresident owe when selling in Galloway Township?
faqs.a: At least 2% of the deed consideration is prepaid at closing as estimated New Jersey gross income tax. The actual figure can be higher, since the formula uses the gain times 10.75%, and the seller can claim a refund after filing a nonresident return.

faqs.q: Is Galloway Township in the Pinelands?
faqs.a: In part. Galloway is within the Pinelands National Reserve, and parts of it are in the state-designated Pinelands Area. Ask the Community Development office about your specific parcel.
